subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should canonical memory-triggered writes to memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md fail closed by default with built-in bounds, scaffold rejection, duplicate skipping, and telemetry, while deferring external validator hooks?
rationale: The fix changes persisted session-memory behavior during upgrades, and the broader hook idea would add a command/plugin security boundary that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Accept strict built-in guard
options.body: Land or adapt the linked PR so daily-memory memory-flush payloads are bounded and rejected or skipped before mutation by default, without adding external command hooks.

options.title: Request compatible rollout
options.body: Ask for the same guard behind an explicit opt-in or staged migration if maintainers are not ready to make fail-closed daily-memory flushing the default.

options.title: Split hook design
options.body: Keep the built-in guard narrow and open a separate security-reviewed design for any post-write validator or plugin hook surface.

recommendation.title: Accept strict built-in guard
recommendation.body: Land or adapt the linked PR so daily-memory memory-flush payloads are bounded and rejected or skipped before mutation by default, without adding external command hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory-flush feature and memory-plugin ownership history point to Peter Steinberger as the clearest product-direction owner for this boundary.
